newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes soft on pre-weekend dlr cover.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes soft on pre-weekend dlr cover.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed weaker on Friday due to late demand to cover dollar positions prior to the weekend, traders said.
"You can't go short, because that's too risky...those who hadn't squared positions stepped in to buy dollars in the last half-hour," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 1.1 and two centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.7280/7.7340 and 7.7230/7.7280 per dollar.
The same-day peso earlier closed three centavos firmer at 7.7120/7.7170 per dollar.
Trade was moderate during the session in contrast to the panic-stricken sessions seen earlier this week.
"The market was mixed and very calm...people bought and sold dollars with no clear trend, because there is no clear consensus yet as to where the peso should be trading," said a trader.
The 48-hour peso closed the week 5.4 centavos weaker than last week's close of 7.6750/7.6800 per dollar.
Traders said that the result of next week's primary Cetes auction would be crucial for the peso.
